strengths: Emits a routing envelope only; refuses to manufacture domain analysis to justify a route.

findings.issue: Overlap 0.381 with ui-task-routing-and-governance and neither names the other as an anti-trigger, so a UI request can be routed by the generic intake or vice versa.
findings.recommendation: Add anti-trigger: UI-only scope routes to ui-task-routing-and-governance; this Skill handles cross-domain or unclassified intake.

findings.issue: Cited sources are an AI product checklist and AI strategy questions, unrelated to request intake or routing; the Skill has no source technique behind it.
findings.recommendation: Re-ground in a routing source or mark as authored; add a concrete routing decision table (stage x risk x authority).

strengths: Scope gate first: returns not-applicable when no UI scope exists.
Separates taste decisions from evidence defects.

findings.issue: The source reviews design by generating visual mockups by default when a designer tool is available ('real visuals, not text descriptions'); the Skill reviews text only and never asks for or references visual artifacts.
findings.recommendation: Add: when mockups or rendered references exist, review against them; otherwise record 'text-only review' as a confidence limit.

findings.issue: No scoring dimensions: the source rates each design area and states what a 10 would look like; the Skill only lists areas.
findings.recommendation: Rate each area 0-10 with the gap to 10 stated as the amendment.

strengths: Journey coverage (setup, first success, debug, upgrade) is right.

findings.issue: Source principle 'gather evidence and force decisions before scoring' starts with target-developer persona interrogation; the Skill has no persona step, so expectations and tolerance are undefined.
findings.recommendation: Add step 1: identify target developer persona and its expectations before tracing journeys.

findings.issue: 'Measurable DX outcomes' is named but no metric (time-to-first-success, steps to hello world, error-to-fix time) is required.
findings.recommendation: Require at least time-to-first-success and failure-recovery criteria.

findings.issue: Both holdouts tie; mutation needs a behavioral challenge.
findings.recommendation: Phase D case with a plan that has a hidden onboarding gap.

strengths: Clear split: governs identity and lifecycle, never authors content.

findings.issue: Sources are document templates, not governance practices; staleness and invalidation rules are authored without source technique.
findings.recommendation: Mark as authored; define a default state set (draft, approved, superseded, stale, retired) and staleness triggers.

strengths: One Diataxis type per document; no unverified present-tense claims.

findings.issue: The source's most important step, codebase archaeology before writing (map structure, read entry points, trace flows), is reduced to 'build a source map from approved facts'; for code documentation the Skill does not instruct reading the code.
findings.recommendation: Add a research step: when documenting code, read entry points and trace the documented flow before drafting.
Phase D case requiring type-pure how-to without explanation drift.

strengths: Independent evidence before convergence; no manufactured consensus.

findings.issue: The workshop-facilitation interaction protocol (entry modes guided/context-dump/best-guess, one question per turn, progress labels, pause/resume, numbered recommendations) is the source's facilitation source of truth and is absent.
findings.recommendation: Add the protocol as the default for AI-facilitated sessions.

findings.issue: The source task format (exact files to create/modify with line ranges, failing test first, exact command with expected failure, bite-sized steps for a zero-context engineer) is reduced to 'map tasks to affected areas'; the gate even forbids 'inventing file paths as facts' without requiring verified paths.
findings.recommendation: Require verified file paths, a failing-test-first step and an exact verification command per task.

findings.issue: Both holdouts tie and mutation needs a behavioral challenge.
findings.recommendation: Phase D: score plans on zero-context executability.

strengths: Decision classification (mechanical/taste/one-way door) faithful to source.

findings.issue: Out-of-scope list with rationale and dependency section from the PRD source are not required outputs.

strengths: Prior authorization or tool availability is never current permission.

findings.issue: Risk classification has no scale (likelihood x impact or reversibility tiers), so dispositions are not reproducible.
findings.recommendation: Define reversibility tiers and the disposition each tier forces.

findings.issue: Close to ai-safety-and-action-governance without an anti-trigger.

findings.issue: Duplicates the role of the released V2 router and composite Recipes (select, sequence, gate, invalidate). An atomic Skill that orchestrates contradicts the decision that workflows live in Recipes.

cross_skill_findings.issue: Three routing-shaped Skills plus the V2 router; ownership of 'which capability next' is split four ways.
cross_skill_findings.recommendation: Router owns Recipe selection; context-intake owns cross-domain classification; ui-task-routing owns UI-only classification; orchestration only for uncovered workflows.

cross_skill_findings.issue: Five plan reviewers; boundaries are sound but only partially cross-referenced.
